questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to BENEVOLENT.
questions.explanation: C is correct. BENEVOLENT = well-meaning and kindly disposed (from Latin: bene = good + volens = wishing). Antonym: malevolent (wishing harm). Usage: 'The benevolent donor gave generously to the orphanage.'

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to ELOQUENT.
questions.explanation: B is correct. ELOQUENT = fluent, persuasive, and expressive in speech or writing. ARTICULATE = able to speak clearly and effectively. Both imply effective verbal communication. Note: 'fluent' implies only smoothness, while 'eloquent' additionally implies persuasiveness.

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to OBSOLETE.
questions.explanation: B is correct. OBSOLETE = no longer used or needed; fallen into disuse. Synonyms: outdated, antiquated, archaic, outmoded. Usage: 'The fax machine has become largely obsolete in the digital age.'

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to LACONIC.
questions.explanation: C is correct. LACONIC = using very few words; brief and concise in speech (from Laconia/Sparta, whose citizens were famously terse). Usage: 'His laconic reply — just 'No' — ended the discussion.' Synonyms: terse, succinct, pithy, concise.

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to PRODIGAL.
questions.explanation: B is correct. PRODIGAL = spending money or resources freely and recklessly; wasteful. Biblical reference: 'The Prodigal Son' wasted his inheritance. Synonyms: extravagant, profligate, spendthrift. Antonym: frugal, thrifty.

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to INSIPID.
questions.explanation: C is correct. INSIPID = lacking flavour, dull and uninteresting. Used for both food (tasteless) and personality/speech (uninspiring). Synonyms: vapid, inane, banal, wishy-washy. Usage: 'The speech was insipid — not a single original thought.'

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to AUGMENT.
questions.explanation: C is correct. AUGMENT = to make greater by adding something; to enhance or increase. (From Latin augere = to grow.) Synonyms: enhance, boost, amplify, supplement. Usage: 'She took a part-time job to augment her income.'

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to IMPETUOUS.
questions.explanation: B is correct. IMPETUOUS = acting or done quickly and without thought; rashly impulsive. Synonyms: rash, reckless, hasty, precipitate. Antonym: deliberate, cautious. Usage: 'His impetuous decision to quit his job without a backup plan proved costly.'

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to PERNICIOUS.
questions.explanation: D is correct. PERNICIOUS = having a harmful effect, especially in a gradual or subtle way (from Latin perniciosus = destructive). Stronger than 'harmful' — implies insidious damage. Synonyms: deleterious, detrimental, injurious. Usage: 'The pernicious effects of misinformation on public health are well-documented.'

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to OBSEQUIOUS.
questions.explanation: C is correct. OBSEQUIOUS = excessively compliant or fawning; attempting to win favour through excessive flattery. Synonyms: sycophantic, servile, unctuous, subservient. Antonym: assertive, defiant. Usage: 'The obsequious assistant agreed with everything his boss said, however absurd.' Often appears with negative connotation in exam passages.
